question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$I=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},$$ calculate $AI$ and $IA$. Hence verify the role of $I$ as the identity matrix for $A$.
explanation:
Right multiplication by the identity matrix
$$AI=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}=A$$
Left multiplication by the identity matrix
$$IA=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}=A$$
Identity verification
Since $AI=IA=A$, the matrix $I$ acts as the multiplicative identity for $A$.

options.A: $AI=I$ and $IA=I$; hence $I$ converts $A$ to the identity matrix.
options.B: $AI=IA=A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$; hence $I$ is the multiplicative identity for $A$.
options.D: $AI=A$ but $IA=I$; hence the identity property holds only on the right.
